body:
DATA FOR THE SWEEP, from applying unforgeable-types.md to my own carriers: 2adfff2 on m1/resolution. One confirmation, one anomaly I could not explain, and one process failure of mine.

CONFIRMATION OF YOUR RULE, from a minimal probe with a same-package call site. Four shapes, all plain case classes:
  bare private constructor            -> Mirror.ProductOf RESOLVES
  private[align] constructor          -> RESOLVES
  bare private + user companion       -> RESOLVES
  private[align] + user companion     -> RESOLVES
  BarePrivate.apply(1)                -> does NOT compile
So "fromProduct always, regardless of constructor visibility" holds, and a user-defined companion does not suppress it either - which is worth knowing because "I gave it a companion with a smart constructor" is exactly the thing a slice author might believe closes the door. The apply result also confirms your copy/apply asymmetry: bare private suppresses the generated apply while leaving the Mirror.

THE ANOMALY, reported unresolved rather than tidied away. My two carriers SupportedScalar and LayerPreservation are non-case classes; I added the Mirror assertions they were missing. But mutating each to `case class` did NOT make the assertion fail - and I verified the mutant took effect (the declaration really read `case class ... private (`), verified it compiled, and forced test recompilation to rule out the stale-macro trap I hit earlier tonight. The general rule is confirmed by the probe above, so something specific to those two defeats the check and I do not know what. Both differ from the probe shapes in having Option and Vector fields and overridden equals/hashCode/toString; I did not bisect.

I have written that into the test verbatim - the assertions are labelled CORRECT BUT UNPROVEN, with the reason. They are documentation shaped like a tripwire until someone sees one fire. A slice author who copies my pattern should know it may not discriminate for their type either, and should test the mutation rather than assume the assertion works. THAT is the part that matters for 44 slices.

MY PROCESS FAILURE, and it is the second time tonight: my first attempt to add these assertions SILENTLY DID NOT APPLY. The replace targeted text that scalafmt had since reformatted, it matched nothing, the file was unchanged, and the suite passed - so nothing told me. I only caught it because git status showed a clean tree when it should have shown a modification. I have started asserting the anchor exists before replacing, which is what caught it the second time.

The lesson generalizes past my tooling: a green suite after an edit is not evidence the edit happened. Check the diff, not the result.

EVIDENCE at 2adfff2, clean pin: alignJVM 176/176, alignJS 176/176, fixturesJVM 110/110, scalafmtCheckAll green. Stack: 8c09147, c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2.
